title: A failing notify under tea's spawn helper is seen by nobody
rawReport:
## Summary
tea's new `spawn` helper runs the host's `notify` step on a detached fiber and accepts any error type from it. When `notify` fails, nothing reads the failure. The step's docs do not say so, and the how-to says a failed save "is still a failure".

## What I was doing
Reviewing https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/pull/566 against https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/556, reading `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts` at head eac0df0.

## What I observed
`SpawnSteps.notify` is typed `Effect.Effect<unknown, unknown>`. The finalizer runs it as `Effect.forkDetach(steps.notify)` and never joins the fiber. The usual `notify` is `tell(parent, parentRun, msg)`, which fails with `StoreFailed` when the parent's save fails. Under `spawn` that failure ends a fiber nobody observes. The how-to's "What the helpers guarantee" lists "A failed save is still a failure" among things the host does not guard.

I read this from the code. I did not run it, and I did not check whether Effect logs an unobserved fiber failure at some level.

## Why it matters
A host author may read the how-to as saying a failed save surfaces somewhere when a child stops. It might not. The parent's own run may still report the failed save through its own `onError`, so the cost may be small.

## Pointers
- `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts` (`SpawnSteps.notify`, the finalizer in `spawn`)
- `packages/tea/docs/how-to/run-many-machines.md`, "What the helpers guarantee"
- https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/556, https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/pull/566

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
A guess: say in the `notify` TSDoc that its failure is dropped, or type it `Effect<unknown>` so the host has to handle the error itself. The second changes a stable signature.

enriched:
## In plain words

When a child machine stops, tea's `spawn` helper runs the host's `notify` step in the background and never looks at how it ended. If `notify` fails, for example because the parent could not save, nobody finds out. The how-to reads as if that failure shows up somewhere. The helpers are not published yet, so we can still change the type for free, and the founder has to pick between a doc sentence and a type change.

## What is wrong

Read at `origin/main` (ccaa4f2):

- `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts:84` types the step as `readonly notify: Effect.Effect<unknown, unknown>`, so it accepts any failure.
- `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts:127` runs it as `Effect.forkDetach(steps.notify)` inside the scope finalizer. Nothing joins or observes that fiber.
- Every example passes `notify: tell(parent, parentRun, msg)`. `tell` fails with `Err | StoreFailed` (`children.ts:45`).
- `packages/tea/docs/how-to/run-many-machines.md`, "What the helpers guarantee", says "A failed save is still a failure. `tell` fails with `StoreFailed` when the parent's save fails." That is true of `tell` called directly. Under `spawn` the same failure ends a fiber nobody reads.
- The `notify` TSDoc says it runs "on a fiber of its own that the closing scope never waits for". It does not say what happens to a failure.

So a host that copies the page's `spawnWorker` loses the parent's failed save on `child_stopped` without a trace.

## The choice the founder has to make

This is a real choice about the public type, so triage did not pick. `./effect` is a `stable` entry in `packages/tea/MAINTAINING.md`, and the helpers ship first in 0.20.0 (https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/pull/572, held as a draft). Until that release goes out, changing `SpawnSteps` costs no semver. After it, option B is a breaking change.

- **A. Say it in the docs.** Keep the type. The `notify` TSDoc and the how-to say a failure of `notify` is dropped, and that a host who cares handles it inside `notify`. Cheapest. The page's one-liner `notify: tell(...)` keeps compiling and keeps dropping the failed save, so the trap stays and only a careful reader avoids it.
- **B. Make the type refuse a failure.** Type it `Effect.Effect<unknown>`, with no error. `notify: tell(...)` then stops compiling, and the host must write what happens to the failure (log it, send it somewhere, or turn it into a defect). The mistake becomes a compile error. Cost: the how-to and both examples get an extra line per `spawn`, and every host has to decide.
- **C. `spawn` reports the failure itself.** A new step or a sink on `spawn` that is handed the failure. This adds API to helpers that were ruled to stay plain functions (https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/554, R1.1 and R2.1).

Triage note: I would pick B, about 70% sure. It costs nothing today and is breaking after the release, and it turns a silent loss into a compile error. The trade-off is a longer copy-paste example. Under any option, a defect inside `notify` still ends the detached fiber unseen, so the TSDoc has to say that too.

## What to change

Common to every option:

- `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts`: the `notify` TSDoc on `SpawnSteps`, and the `spawn` TSDoc, say what happens when `notify` fails.
- `packages/tea/docs/how-to/run-many-machines.md`: the `notify` bullet in step 2 and the "A failed save is still a failure" bullet say the same thing the code does under `spawn`.
- `packages/tea/src/effect/children.test.ts`: a test pins that behaviour.
- `packages/tea/docs/reference/effect.md`: regenerated with `pnpm --filter @demlik/tea docs:reference`, never hand-edited.

Under B, also: the `notify` type in `children.ts`, the `spawn` TSDoc example, the two `spawn` calls in the how-to (steps 2 and 4), `packages/tea/examples/parent-and-workers-effect.ts`, `packages/tea/examples/process-tree-effect.ts`, and the `hostOf` helper's `notify` parameter in `children.test.ts`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A host that spawns three children under a parent whose store fails every save, then stops all three, can learn that each notice failed by a route the `notify` TSDoc names: a test in `packages/tea/src/effect/children.test.ts` runs that fixture and asserts the three failures are seen where the docs say they are (or, under option A, asserts that they are dropped and that a host handler written inside `notify` sees all three).
- [ ] The TSDoc on `SpawnSteps.notify` in `packages/tea/src/effect/children.ts` says in one sentence what happens to a failure of `notify`, and in one sentence that a defect in it is not observed by `spawn`.
- [ ] `packages/tea/docs/how-to/run-many-machines.md` no longer lets a reader think a failed parent save surfaces on its own when a child stops: the "A failed save is still a failure" bullet and the step 2 `notify` bullet match the code's behaviour under `spawn`.
- [ ] If the ruling is option B: `SpawnSteps.notify` is typed `Effect.Effect<unknown>`, and a type-level test shows `notify: tell(parent, parentRun, msg)` with no error handling is a compile error.
- [ ] If the ruling is option B: every `spawn` call in the how-to, in `packages/tea/examples/parent-and-workers-effect.ts` and in `packages/tea/examples/process-tree-effect.ts` handles the failure of `tell` in the open, and the page mirror test `packages/tea/src/effect/many-machines-how-to.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] If the ruling is option A: `SpawnSteps.notify` keeps its current type, and the how-to shows one short example of a host handling the failure inside `notify`.
- [ ] `packages/tea/docs/reference/effect.md` is regenerated and its `SpawnSteps` entry carries the new TSDoc.
- [ ] A changeset for `@demlik/tea` describes the change.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass from the root.

## Triage notes

Triage note: the original was unsure whether Effect logs a failure nobody observes. At `effect` 4.0.0-rc.117, the one such report I found is `UnhandledLogLevel` in `References.ts`, and its only reader is the pool finalizer in `Pool.ts`. I found no log for a detached fiber that fails. I read the source; I did not run it.

Triage note: the original guessed the parent's own run "may still report the failed save through its own `onError`". The save-failure test in `packages/tea/src/effect/run.test.ts` (near line 567) ends with `expect(reports).toEqual([])`: a failed save fails the `dispatch` and is not handed to `onError`. So the dispatch's caller is the only one told, and under `spawn` that caller is the detached fiber. The loss is real, not small.

Triage note: typed `type:bug`, not `type:decision`. The deliverable is a fix that ships, and the choice above is one question inside it. The audience is `ready-for:human` until that question is ruled.

Triage note: standalone. I searched the board for the spawn, tell and stop helpers and for a dropped notify failure. https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/556 and https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/567 own this surface and are closed. https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/554 is the grilling session, not a work ticket. No open issue absorbs it.

Triage note: file overlap. https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/579 edits the import lines of steps 2 and 3 in `packages/tea/docs/how-to/run-many-machines.md`, the same page this issue edits, and under option B this issue also edits the step 2 code block. Whichever lands second rebases. https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/569 says it does not edit that page; it only links to it.

Triage note: priced `p1`. The founder said in conversation on 2026-10-04 (relayed to triage, not a recorded ruling) that he wants this fixed before 0.20.0 goes out, and option B is only free until then. No package here has a signed-out visitor, so the visitor rule does not apply.
